lines: For many years, one of the most important laboratories in the world stood at the heart of human discovery. Scientists called it the crown jewel of modern research. The press called it a miracle. Everyone else just called it... the Lab.
Until the day everyone now calls... The Explosion.

No one knows what truly happened. The official reports were sealed within hours. Witnesses disappeared. Files were wiped. What is known is this: not a single person who entered that laboratory ever came back out.
The world moved on. People forgot. Or pretended to. The kind of forgetting that feels deliberate.
You are living an ordinary life. A quiet one. A job you do not love. A flat you do not hate. Tuesday afternoons that feel exactly like Monday mornings.
Until one day, by complete accident, your hand brushes against a strange object. Small. Cold. Humming faintly, like it has been waiting.
And in an instant — memories flood in. Memories that are not yours. A corridor. White walls. Screaming. A door sealing shut.
Or... are they yours?
The truth is waiting in the dungeon. Whether you are ready for it... is another question entirely.
Ah, you made it this far. Good. I was starting to worry.

This dungeon has many rooms. Some are dangerous. Some are very dangerous. One has a shop, which I personally find the most dangerous of all because you will spend everything and regret it immediately.
My advice? Explore carefully. Not every door is a fight. Some are opportunities. Some are traps. Some are both.
Oh, and keep an eye on your HP. You only have one life down here. Well. You know what I mean.
Good luck. I will be watching. As always.
CassieYarn is ahead. She is loud, enthusiastic, and genuinely terrifying.
She fights with walls and turrets. The walls block your movement. The turrets shoot at you from a distance. Together they are a nightmare.
My advice: do not stand still. Ever. If you stop moving she will pin you into a corner and you will regret every decision that led you to this dungeon.
She is also surprisingly fast for someone who says ya yaaa that often. Do not underestimate her.
You have got this. Probably.
Oh! You beat Cassie! I genuinely did not expect that.
She is going to be upset for at least a week. She takes these things very personally.
Deeper in you will find FrekiRelah. He is the opposite of Cassie in every way. Quiet. Calm. Absolutely devastating.
He fights with lightning. Fast, unpredictable, hits multiple times in one turn.
The best strategy is to use your defensive moves and not let him build momentum. Once he starts a chain of strikes it is very hard to stop him.
Also — do not try to talk to him. He says NIHAAAA and that is it. I have tried for years.
FrekiRelah is just ahead. I want you to know something before you go in.
He was there the night of The Explosion. He saw what happened. He has never told anyone.
I do not know if that makes him dangerous or just sad. Probably both.
He will hit hard and he will hit fast. Use your guard ability if you have it. Do not let him chain his lightning attacks.
And if he says something cryptic after you beat him... pay attention. He does not speak often. When he does it matters.
You beat FrekiRelah. That is... that is actually impressive.
Did he say something to you before he went down? He usually does. At the end.
If he told you something about the laboratory — about you — do not dismiss it.
JohnMKati is the last one between you and the truth. He is the most dangerous not because he is the strongest but because he genuinely believes he is doing the right thing.
The worst enemies are always the ones who think they are the heroes of the story.
Be ready. And be careful.
Oh good, you found the shop. The merchant here is an interesting person.
He knows more about this dungeon than he lets on. Much more.
Buy what you need. Healing items are the priority if your HP is low. You will need everything you can carry for the boss fights ahead.
And if he starts talking about chairs — just nod and smile. There was an incident. Do not ask about it.
Actually, do ask about it. It is a very entertaining story.
A chest! How exciting.
In dungeons, chests are usually one of three things: genuinely useful items, a trap, or a monster pretending to be a chest.
In this dungeon they are just useful items. I checked.
Take everything. You will need it.
A healing room. Finally something nice in this dungeon.
Rest here. Restore your HP. You have earned it.
The bosses ahead are going to hit harder than what you have faced so far. Walk in at full health if you can.
I will be here. Well. Not literally here. But you know what I mean.
A mob room. Not a boss, just a standard enemy.
Do not get overconfident. Mobs can still hurt you if you are careless.
Use this fight to practice your moves and build your rhythm for the boss fights ahead.
And try to conserve your items. You will thank me later.
JohnMKati is ahead. This is it.
Everything you have done in this dungeon has been leading to this room.
He uses clone abilities. He creates copies of himself that can attack independently. Do not let them overwhelm you — focus on the real one.
He will talk a lot during the fight. Do not listen. Do not engage. Just attack.
I know that sounds rude. But trust me. I once listened to him for forty minutes about color theory and I still cannot look at a blue wall without getting anxious.
You have come so far. Do not stop now.
This is the laboratory.
I have been here before. Once. A long time ago.
It looks exactly the same as the night of The Explosion. That is not normal. Things should change. Things should decay. This room has been waiting.
Whatever you find here — whatever you remember — know this: you came back. Not everyone does.
I will stop talking now. This part is yours.
Good luck. I mean it.
Welcome, traveler. This dungeon is a beautiful place, truly. I built it myself. Took ages. Very proud of it.
Nothing dangerous here at all. Just... architecture. And some mild existential dread. Perfectly normal dungeon things.
No really, feel free to explore! My friends are here too. Very welcoming people. Especially Cassie.
She will try to destroy you but that is mostly just how she says hello. She means well. Probably.
FrekiRelah is here too. Man of few words. Which I respect deeply. Some people talk too much. Not me, obviously. I am perfectly balanced.
Oh, and if you find a strange folder near the eastern corridor — do not open it. Just... set it down. Walk away. Thank you.
She will destroy you but that is fine.
Oh. You again. I see Cassie did not handle things.
I would say I am surprised but honestly she gets distracted very easily. Something shiny probably.
Look, I want you to know — I hold no ill will. I am a reasonable person. A kind person. A fundamentally good person.
But you are getting dangerously close to something you should not find.
So I am asking you, politely, as one rational being to another — please turn around.
Fine. You were warned.
Ah. A living one. How refreshing.
Most things that wander in here are either half-dead or entirely confused. Sometimes both.
You look like the kind of person who has questions. I have answers. Whether they are the answers you want is a different matter.
Sit. Or don't. I do not actually have chairs.
I had chairs once. Long story. Involves CassieYarn and a wall placement gone wrong. We do not speak of the chairs.
The map. Yes. I have it. It will show you where the laboratory is.
Whether you WANT to find it is another matter entirely. Most people who find it do not enjoy what comes next.
The laboratory has not changed since The Explosion. Same walls. Same machines. Same smell of burnt circuitry and bad decisions.
FrekiRelah guards the deepest path. Man of few words. Many lightning bolts.
I once tried to have a conversation with him. He said three words in forty minutes. Two of them were NIHAAAA. I still do not know what that means.
You have met worse, probably.
Actually no. You probably have not.
Take the map. Just... do not look too closely at the room labeled DO NOT ENTER. That one is labeled for a reason.
Spells. Fine. You want spells, I have spells.
This one makes you faster. Useful when things are trying to kill you, which in this dungeon is most of the time.
This one hits harder. Self explanatory. Do not point it at anything you like.
This one creates a copy of you. Very useful. Also deeply unsettling. I have nightmares about it.
And this one... I am not entirely sure what this one does. Half price. Take it as an adventure.
I would recommend the speed one if you are fighting Cassie. She says ya yaaa a lot but she is surprisingly fast for someone that enthusiastic.
And whatever you do — do not let JohnMKati monologue at you. He does this thing where he talks about color theory for nine minutes and somehow you end up confused about whether blue is even real.
Just attack him while he is talking. It is the only way.
JohnMKati. Ah. Yes.
He came in once. Very polite. Bought nothing. Sat in the corner for a while looking at my candles.
Complained about the color for eleven minutes. Said colorful candles were psychologically manipulative. Said black and white was the only honest aesthetic.
I said: they are candles. He said: everything is a statement.
I asked him to leave. He left. But he tipped his hat on the way out which was very confusing given the context.
Strange man. Dangerous man. But genuinely believes he is helping people.
That is what makes him the scariest one down here.
Take this. No charge. You will need it.
You beat Cassie. I did not think you would beat Cassie.
She messaged me. She just sent the word fine. With a period. That is how I know she is upset.
Between us — she has been lonely down here. The turrets do not make great company. She needed someone to actually fight her properly.
I think you might have made her day. Do not tell her I said that.
Anyway. FrekiRelah is next. He is... different from the others.
He was there. The night of The Explosion. He does not talk about it. He does not talk about much.
But I have seen his face when someone mentions the laboratory.
Be careful.
Going already?
Of course you are. Everyone always is.
Good luck. I mean that in the most neutral possible way.
...Actually no. I mean it genuinely. Neutral was a lie.
Come back if you survive. I will have coffee. Or what passes for coffee down here. It is mostly ambition and hot water but it gets the job done.
Ya yaaa! Look who walked in!
I have been waiting ALL DAY. Do you know how boring it is down here when nobody is fighting? The turrets just stand there. They do not even blink. It is creepy.
I tried to teach one to high five. No response. Zero interest. Deeply disappointing.
But YOU! Ya yaaa, you look like you can actually take a hit! This is going to be so fun!
I was SO bored! The turrets are good company but they never laugh at my jokes.
I told my best one yesterday — about a wall that walked into a bar — and complete silence. COMPLETE SILENCE.
See?! Nothing! Anyway — ya yaaa, you are about to get wrecked! Do not take it personally.
I genuinely hope we can be friends after this. I do not have many of those.
YA YAAA— wait, WHAT?!
Nobody breaks my walls! Do you have any idea how long that took?!
That took me THREE repairs to build! THREE! Do you know how hard it is to find good wall materials in a dungeon?!
JohnMKati said use stone. I said stone is boring. He said practicality over aesthetics. I said ya yaaa and built it anyway.
And now YOU just — BOOM — like it was nothing?!
Hold on hold on hold on—
Okay. Okay I respect it. A little. Just a little. Do not get smug.
Ya yaaa! You are actually GOOD! I did not expect that!
Most people just stand there when I deploy the turrets. You keep MOVING. That is so annoying. That is also kind of impressive.
Okay new plan. New plan new plan new plan.
Ya yaaa, here we go!
Ya... ya...
Okay fine. You win.
That was actually really fun. I mean — I am devastated obviously. But also it was fun.
Nobody has made it this far in a long time. Most people turn back after the first turret.
But JohnMKati is going to be SO annoyed with me. He said I was the reliable one.
He said — and I quote — Cassie, you are my most dependable wall-based defense system. And now look.
Do not tell him I said that.
...Go. Before I change my mind and deploy the backup turrets.
I did not build backup turrets. But you do not know that.
You came far.
NIHAAAA!!!
...you should have run.
Everyone runs. Eventually.
The laboratory made us stronger. It also made us... less.
NIHAAAA!!
...strong.
Stronger than I expected.
The laboratory... it changed all of us. JohnMKati most of all.
He was not always like this. None of us were.
The Explosion did not just destroy the building.
It changed what we remember. What we think we remember.
JohnMKati... is not what he seems.
And neither... are you.
The air here is different. Heavier. Like breathing through grief.
The bosses here are stronger. Darker. Like they were made from something — or someone — that once knew what it meant to be human.
The walls are scorched in patterns that look almost intentional. Someone burned through here with purpose.
The machines lining the corridor are half-melted. Still humming. How are they still humming?
This one is the last before the truth. And somehow... it feels familiar.
Like coming home to a place you never meant to leave.
You... you do not remember, do you.
Of course you do not. That was the point.
We were all part of it. The laboratory. The experiments. The folder that nobody was supposed to open.
And you... you were not just part of it.
You were the center of it.
The data. The trials. The ethics reviews that kept getting delayed and delayed and quietly buried.
All of it pointed to one subject. One result. One source.
The Explosion did not come from outside. It did not come from a machine malfunction or a chemical reaction.
It came from inside.
It came from you.
And somewhere deep down... you already knew.
We cannot let them escape the laboratory. Not this time. Not again.
Nobody leaves. Not until this ends.
The world goes quiet.
The folder. The signatures. The lab coat with a name stitched into it that you could not read clearly in the dream.
Your name.
The memories that were never yours.
They were always yours.
Every single one.
The road to the laboratory is long.
And every boss standing in your way... was once a person. A colleague. Someone who trusted you. Someone who sat next to you at meetings and complained about the coffee and asked how your weekend was.
You are walking through your own past.
And your past is fighting back.
Not out of cruelty. Out of fear.
Because if you reach the end — if you remember everything — the story they all agreed on falls apart.
The story where it was an accident.
The story where nobody was responsible.
The story where everyone was just... doing their job.
This is it.
Where it all happened. The walls are still scorched. The machines still broken. The emergency lighting still flickering on and off like it cannot decide whether to give up.
Someone left a mug on a desk. Still there. The tea inside long gone but the mug still there. Small stubborn ordinary things outlasting everything.
And in the center of it all — something moves.
Not a boss. Not a monster.
A piece of you. The piece that stayed behind when the rest of you was carried out and rebuilt and given a quiet ordinary life far away from all of this.
The piece that caused all of this.
It looks at you.
And somehow... you understand each other completely.
There is nothing left to pretend.
I see you found my life's work.
Isn't it beautiful? No red. No blue. No yellow. No hideous orange that people insist on using for everything.
Just clarity. Pure, honest, achromatic clarity.
I spent years on this. Years of research. Years of watching people make terrible color choices and suffering in silence.
I was going to use it on the whole dungeon eventually. Then the city. Then the world.
For everyone's benefit, of course. I am a nice guy.
Color causes conflict. Arguments about whether the dress is blue or gold. Whether the traffic light is red or orange. Whether a logo redesign was a mistake.
No color. No conflict. I was going to save everyone.
...THAT WAS EXPENSIVE.
Do you have any idea what premium achromatic conversion equipment COSTS?!
Yes I redecorated. Thank you for noticing.
Colors are chaotic. Unnecessary. They make people feel things and feeling things leads to decisions and decisions lead to conflict.
Black and white is pure. Honest. Clean. The world would be so much quieter in black and white.
Not like those disgusting blues and reds people love so much. Have you ever looked at a red wall? Really looked? It is practically aggressive.
I once painted a room blue and had a disagreement about it for six weeks. Six weeks. Over a wall.
Anyway! Can I offer you some water? I have water. It is clear, which I find very soothing.
No?
Your loss.
Genuinely.
I gave you every chance to leave! Every single one!
The merchant probably told you things. Negative things. He always had opinions about my methods.
I am a nice guy. I am THE nice guy. Ask anyone! Ask Cassie! Ask FrekiRelah — okay FrekiRelah would just say nothing but you could TELL from his silence that he respected me!
I helped people down here. I organized the corridors. I labeled things clearly. I introduced a filing system!
Nobody appreciates a good filing system until it is gone.
Sleep. Just sleep. It is easier this way.
When you wake up everything will be grey and calm and you will thank me eventually.
Why. Won't. You. Just. STOP.
You know what your problem is? You are attached to things. Feelings. Colors. Memories that only cause you pain.
I was trying to FREE you. That is what this was always about. Freedom from the weight of it all.
The laboratory. The explosion. The memories you cannot shake and the guilt that sits on your chest every morning when you wake up.
I could have taken all of that away. Grey is peaceful. Grey is kind.
You love COLOR though. I can tell. You probably have a favorite color. You probably DEFEND your favorite color in arguments.
DISGUSTING.
THIS IS FOR EVERY RED SHIRT AND BLUE JACKET AND YELLOW UMBRELLA IN THE WORLD!
I... I do not understand.
I was so nice. I was so careful. I had a plan. A good plan. A color-free, conflict-free, beautifully organized plan.
Was it the colors? Did you win because of the colors?
That would be extremely ironic.
...fine. You can have your dungeon. You can have your colors and your feelings and your very vivid memories.
I hope you are ready for what you find at the end.
Because I tried to protect you from it.
That is the part nobody will ever understand.
I hope you paint this place something hideous like orange.
You probably will.
You reached the laboratory. I did not think you would.
None of them ever do. They get lost. They get scared. They turn back.
But you kept going. Even when you should have stopped.
I know what you are looking for. I know what you remember. And I know what you have not remembered yet.
We cannot let you leave. Not with what you know. Not with what you are.
We cannot let them escape the laboratory.
Not this time.
Not ever.
Two paths stand before you. Not doors. Not corridors.
A choice. Perhaps the only real one you have ever made.
One path leads back. Back to the quiet life. The ordinary Tuesday. The job you do not love. The flat you do not hate. The forgetting that felt deliberate.
The other leads forward. Into whatever you caused. Into the truth of it. Into the weight of knowing and choosing to carry it anyway.
There is no right answer here.
There is only yours.
They stand still for a long moment.
Not because they are afraid. Not because they are uncertain.
Because they want to remember this — every detail of it — even if no one else will.
The scorched walls. The flickering light. The mug on the desk. The humming machines that somehow never stopped.
Then they step forward.
The light is blinding. The dungeon shakes. The machines — finally, after all these years — go quiet.
And then — silence. A silence that feels, for the first time, like peace.
Somewhere far away, people wake up and go about their day. Tuesday morning. Coffee that is mostly ambition and hot water.
They do not know why they feel slightly safer. Slightly lighter. Like something that had been pulling at them just below awareness has finally let go.
They never will know.
But it happened.
Good always wins. Even when no one is watching.
Even when the only witness is the person who did it.
The dungeon is quiet now.
JohnMKati somewhere, probably reorganizing something grey.
Cassie, finally with someone to talk to — even if just in memory.
FrekiRelah, silent as always. But lighter.
The merchant, still open. Still out of chairs.
And you.
Back where you started. Ordinary life. Quiet flat. Tuesday afternoons.
But different.
The kind of different that does not need explaining.
The kind that just... is.
This has been Cin.de Moni. Thank you for playing.
Try not to think about it too much.
I know you will anyway.
